attributes.body_ja:
「ても構（かま）わない」は、「(A) てもいい」「(A) ても気（き）にしない」「(A) でも問題（もんだい）ない」という意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。この文法（ぶんぽう）は、「ても」（動詞（どうし）とイ形容詞（けいようし）の場合（ばあい））または「でも」（名詞（めいし）とナ形容詞（けいようし）の場合）に、五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「構（かま）う」の否定形（ひていけい）「構（かま）わない」を合（あ）わせてできています。

「ても構（かま）わない」は、「ても」と「でも」につなげられるものであれば、どんな語（ご）でも使（つか）えます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「構（かま）う」に使（つか）われている漢字（かんじ）「構（こう）」には、何（なに）かに備（そな）えて姿勢（しせい）を取（と）ったり、準備（じゅんび）をしたりするという意味（いみ）があります。この文法（ぶんぽう）の「ても構（かま）わない」は、そのように備（そな）える必要（ひつよう）はない、気（き）にしなくてもいいという気持（きも）ちを表（あらわ）していると考（かんが）えてもいいでしょう。
attributes.body:
ても構（かま）わない is often used to express that something 'doesn't matter', or that the speaker 'doesn't mind'. This structure is a combination of ても (with verbs and い-Adjectives), or でも (with nouns and な-Adjectives) grouped with the negative conjugation of the う - Verb 構（かま）う, which means 'to brace'. Literally, this expression can be thought of as being similar to 'to not be uptight'. However, it is almost always simply used to convey that there is no issue with something.

ても構（かま）わない may be used with any type of word that appears in its ても or でも conjugation form.

Fun Fact

構（かま）う is usually translated as 'to brace', but the kanji 構（かま） often has the nuance of 'to posture', or 'to pose' (into some type of strong/resistant shape). In the ても構（かま）わない grammar structure, this translates as (A) simply being something that will not cause the speaker to 'posture', 'position', or 'pose' themselves in a resistant way.

attributes.description: The difference between なくてもいい and てもかまわない
Saying something is ok to do or not do

attributes.body: Both Verb + てもいい and てもかまわない are used to give or ask for permission. The difference is tone and formality. てもいい is a basic, everyday expression, while てもかまわない is slightly more formal and often used in writing or professional contexts to mean 'It doesn't matter if…' or 'It's fine if…'

attributes.body: Both てもいい and てもかまわない are used to give or ask for permission, but with slight differences in nuance and tone. てもいい is a straightforward way to say 'It's okay' or 'Is it okay to (do this?)' On the other hand, てもかまわない adds a nuance of 'Do you mind if…' or 'it doesn't matter if…' てもかまわない sounds more polite, especially in it's かまいません form.

attributes.body: でよければ and てもかまわない both express acceptance, but from different perspectives. でよければ is most often used to modestly present something as an option, e.g. 私でよければお手伝いします ('If I'm acceptable, I'll help'). In contrast, てもかまわない is used to allow or grant permission, e.g. 使ってもかまわない ('I don't mind if you use it').
